title: lightweight client dependency sweep and vendor stability cleanup
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce noise and risk from transitive dependencies across Python, JS, and Go client libraries and remove a small set of deprecated public parameters. This ticket owns the lightweight sweep: bump safe minors/patches, pin a handful of unstable transitive packages to vetted versions, and deprecate two legacy request fields with a compatibility shim and clear migration docs. We are NOT doing large API surface redesigns here — focus is on safe roll-forward and hygiene that improves build reproducibility and runtime startup latency for edge environments.

Scope:
- Audit current transitive graphs for three client repos (python-client, js-client, go-client) to identify 10 highest-risk packages (by CVE history, semver volatility, and build nondeterminism).
- Apply minimal version pins or ranges in lockfiles/manifest to eliminate known flakiness (no major upgrades unless low risk).
- Remove deprecated request fields "client_context" and "legacy_flags" from SDK surface; provide runtime shim for one release that logs deprecation warnings and maps to new fields.
- Regenerate lockfiles, run full CI including integration tests and performance microbenchmarks.
- Publish migration docs and a deprecation notice in SDK changelogs and Console release notes.

Out of scope:
- Major language-specific client rewrites or large refactors (handled by separate tickets).
- Forced model-runtime dependency upgrades that require kernel work or infra changes.

Success metrics:
- CI build reproducibility across three builds for each client (sha parity or <1 mismatch).
- Reduce failing dependency-related flaky tests by 90% in nightly runs.
- <2% increase in cold-start p95 for client init in microbenchmarks.

Artifacts & links:
- Audit spreadsheet: drive.google.com/sheet/clients-dep-audit-2026
- Draft deprecation doc: confluence.internal/redwood/sdk-deprecations-2026
- PR template for pinned deps: github.com/redwood/sdk/.github/dependency-pin-template.md

Rollout plan:
1) Branch-level pins and lockfile regenerate per repo, run CI in parallel.
2) Deploy runtime shim releases for each language that accept deprecated fields but log warnings (1 patch release).
3) After one weekly release window with no customer reports, remove shim and mark fields removed (minor release).
4) Announce migration window and update public changelogs and Console banner for enterprise customers.
